name: Horseshoe Park Campground
note: The City of Hallock's second campground: a small gravel loop under trees off N Birch Ave just north of downtown, about 1 km from Gilbert Olson. Weekly, monthly and multi-month stays are also sold. Site count, hookups and pad size are not posted. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: hallockmn.org/camping/ (read 2026-10-15, in-repo record audit/price_research/local_mn_2026-10-15/mn_pages.jsonl) has a separate rate column 'Horseshoe Park Campground | DAILY $30 | WEEKLY $150 | MONTHLY $350 | 3-MONTHS $1050' (4-6 month rates also listed) and 'Call City Hall to book your reservation, 218-843-2737'. Google Maps (gm.py, 2026-11-12) has 'Horseshoe Park', 31 N Birch Ave, Hallock, at 48.77694,-96.94557 (about 90 m E of the pin, on Birch Ave beside the loop); 4.3 stars from 6 reviews, phone +1 218-843-2737, website hallockmn.org/camping/, not marked closed. Esri World Imagery 2025-09-28 (WV02, rendered at ~220 m and z19) shows a gravel horseshoe loop at 48.77688,-96.94681 with about 5-6 travel trailers/motorhomes of roughly 30 ft on it (e.g. 48.77690,-96.94709) and a white-roofed building at its SE. Wayback 2024-10-08 also shows the loop with units. So this is a real drive-in city campground where a 23-ft rig fits, with a posted daily rate (public: no price gate).
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-12: Esri World Imagery 2025-09-28 (WV02 0.5 m; export at ~800 m and ~220 m, z19 3x3 stitch) plus Esri Wayback 2024-10-08 (GE01), 2021-03-06 and 2020-04-15 (WV02) at z19, all rendered. The loop sits in a tree clump on mowed town land between N Birch Ave and the rail line/highway, north of downtown. The nearest open water is the South Branch Two Rivers about 450 m E (48.7780,-96.9407), past a road, houses and the wooded city park. The only nearer feature is a dry mowed drainage swale about 40 m N, with no water visible in any frame. No water on or near the sites, so not waterfront. Town flatland, no dam.

fees.note: City of Hallock, Horseshoe Park column: $30 a day, $150 a week, $350 a month, $1,050 for 3 months (4-6 months also sold; 20% off multi-month stays paid by June 1). Call City Hall to book.

flags: Long-stay share: the city sells 1-6 month stays (20% off if paid by June 1) next to the $30 daily rate. No site count exists, so the 1-in-10 nightly test can't be counted. The 2025-09-28 frame shows about 5-6 units, several with boats or vehicles beside them, which looks like monthly campers. The pre-season frames 2020-04-15 (one unit, at the Birch Ave end) and 2021-03-06 (none, snow) show empty pads, so units are not stored year-round. Kept as a public city campground with a posted daily rate and phone booking. A phone check of the nightly share is worth doing.

Hookups unconfirmed and left absent. The record's '30- and 50-amp hookups' sentence precedes the Gilbert Olson column and may describe that park. Web-search summaries of the refused page say Horseshoe has water, sewer and electric, but they were not read directly. The Dyrt (auto-generated, calls it 'county-managed', which is wrong) lists electric/50 A/showers/dump/'RVs up to 50 feet'; it was not used.
Site count and pad size not posted. Rig fit is from imagery (units of roughly 30 ft on the loop), not from a stated limit.

hallockmn.org returned a Cloudflare 403 on one plain fetch 2026-11-12. Explore Minnesota's profile returned a Cloudflare 403 too. Neither was retried. The rate and booking come only from the 2026-10-15 in-repo read, as the reviewer ruled.
Duplicate check: the only DB entry within 20 km is 5633 Gilbert Olson Campground, 1.1 km SE (a different park). There is no Horseshoe entry in MN.
The Dyrt's pin (48.77700,-96.94200) is in the wooded park by the river, about 350 m E of the campground. The pin used here is on the loop itself.
